Name: Useful Hats
Author: byLinnea
Description:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]Hats in Stardew Valley are pure cosmetics. Useful Hats fixes that: every hat in the game now gives a small stat buff while worn, themed to what the hat is. The Fishing Hat helps you fish, and the Hard Hat protects you in the mines. The rarer the hat, the stronger the buff, so that getting those elusive hats is actually worth it.

And on Spirit's Eve, wearing a costume finally means something. Turn up in a mask and the villagers will notice.[/color]

[b][size=4]Installation instructions[/size][/b]
[list=1]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Install the latest version of SMAPI (see the SMAPI page for instructions).[/color][/*]
[*]Download this mod and unzip it into your `Stardew Valley/Mods` folder.[/*]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Run the game via SMAPI.[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]To uninstall, delete the UsefulHats folder from the Mods folder. Hat buffs leave nothing behind. Friendship earned from the Halloween feature is permanent, since it is written to your save like any other friendship, but you can switch that feature off entirely in config.json if you would rather it never happened.[/color]

[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Buffs for every obtainable vanilla hat (120+ of them), themed around each hat's identity and how you earn it.[/*]
[*]Rarity-based balance, depending on how hard the hat is to obtain.[/*]
[*]Visible buff icon with the hat's name while worn.[/*]
[*][b]Halloween costumes:[/b] 43 hats count as costumes. Wear one on Spirit's Eve and the villagers you talk to that day like you a little more, with a bigger bonus from the children.[/*]
[*][b]Villagers react:[/b] 49 handwritten comments on your costume, one per villager, covering the vanilla cast and Stardew Valley Expanded. They stay quiet during the festival itself so they do not interrupt the maze.[/*]
[*]Fully configurable: every stat of every hat lives in `config.json`, and the Halloween feature can be turned off or tuned separately.[/*]
[*]Fully translatable: every line of text the mod shows lives in `i18n/default.json`.[/*]
[*]Works with custom hats from other mods: add an entry with the hat's ID to `config.json,` and it gets a buff too. Press F5 in-game while wearing any hat to log its ID to the SMAPI console.[/*]
[*]Works with multiplayer.[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/color][/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0 or newer[/*]
[/list]No other mods required. Compatible with hat retextures (buffs key on the hat's ID, not its looks). Stardew Valley Expanded is supported if you have it, and ignored if you do not.

[size=4][b]The Halloween costume feature[/b][/size]
[spoiler]On Fall 27, any hat listed as a costume gets an extra line in its tooltip so you know it counts. Wear one that day and the first conversation you have with each villager earns you friendship, with a larger bonus from Vincent, Jas, Leo and Morgan.

Put the costume on [b]before you leave the farm[/b]. Anyone you have already spoken to that morning has had their conversation and will not count.

Most villagers also have something to say about it. Those comments are suppressed during the Spirit's Eve festival so they do not interfere with the maze, though friendship still accrues.

[b]Turning it off or tuning it[/b]
All of this lives in config.json alongside the hat stats:

[list]
[*][b]EnableHalloweenCostumes[/b] (default true): the master switch. Set it to false and the entire feature is gone. Your hat buffs are unaffected.[/*]
[*][b]EnableCostumeDialogue[/b] (default true): set to false to keep the friendship bonus but stop villagers commenting.[/*]
[*][b]CostumeFriendshipPoints[/b] (default 25): points earned per villager. 250 points is one full heart.[/*]
[*][b]CostumeKidFriendshipPoints[/b] (default 50): points earned from anyone listed in CostumeKids.[/*]
[*][b]CostumeKids[/b]: which villagers give the larger bonus. Uses internal names.[/*]
[*][b]CostumeHats[/b]: which hat IDs count as costumes. Same IDs as the Hats list, so F5 works here too.[/*]
[/list]
Want the flavour without the balance change? Leave everything on and set both point values to 0. You keep the comments and the tooltips, and nothing is written to your save.

[b]Rewriting the villager comments[/b]
Every line lives in i18n/default.json, keyed by the villager's internal name:

[code]"costume.dialogue.Penny": "Oh, that's lovely! Jas and Vincent are going to be so excited."[/code]
Change any of them to taste, or add a key for a villager from another mod. Anyone without a line, or with an empty one, falls back to the generic comment, so you can rewrite them at your own pace without breaking anything.

Translations are very welcome. Copy default.json to de.json, fr.json, or any locale code Stardew supports, and translate the values.[/spoiler]
[size=4][b]Changing the values yourself[/b][/size]
[spoiler]Every buff in this mod is read from a plain text file, so you can rebalance anything you like without touching the code.
[b]1. Find the file[/b]
Launch the game through SMAPI at least once. The mod then creates:
[code]Stardew Valley/Mods/UsefulHats/config.json[/code]Open it in any text editor (Notepad, Notepad++, VS Code).
[b]2. Understand the format[/b]
Each entry is one hat ID followed by the stats it grants:
[code]"70": {
       "Farming": 0,
       "Fishing": 0,
       "Mining": 0,
       "Foraging": 0,
       "Luck": 0,
       "Attack": 0,
       "Defense": 0,
       "Speed": 0,
       "MaxStamina": 0,
       "MagneticRadius": 16,
       "Immunity": 1
},[/code]The hat above is the Witch Hat and it grants +1 Immunity and +16 to Magnetic Radius.
[b]3. Available stats[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Farming[/b], [b]Fishing[/b], [b]Mining[/b], [b]Foraging[/b], [b]Luck[/b]: skill levels, use small numbers like 1 or 2[/*]
[*][b]Attack[/b], [b]Defense[/b], [b]Immunity[/b]: combat stats, also small numbers[/*]
[*][b]Speed[/b]: movement speed, 1 is roughly a Coffee, so keep this low[/*]
[*][b]MaxStamina[/b]: extra energy in raw points, 20 to 40 is noticeable[/*]
[*][b]MagneticRadius[/b]: item pickup range in pixels, one tile is 64[/*]
[/list][b]4. Examples[/b]
Make the Straw Hat much stronger:
[code]"4": {
       "Farming": 5,
       "Fishing": 0,
       "Mining": 0,
       "Foraging": 0,
       "Luck": 0,
       "Attack": 0,
       "Defense": 0,
       "Speed": 1,
       "MaxStamina": 0,
       "MagneticRadius": 0,
       "Immunity": 0
},[/code]Give a hat no buff at all, just change all values to zero:
[code]"4": {
       "Farming": 0,
       "Fishing": 0,
       "Mining": 0,
       "Foraging": 0,
       "Luck": 0,
       "Attack": 0,
       "Defense": 0,
       "Speed": 0,
       "MaxStamina": 0,
       "MagneticRadius": 0,
       "Immunity": 0
},[/code]Add a hat that has no entry yet, put it anywhere in the list:
[code]"36": {
       "Farming": 0,
       "Fishing": 0,
       "Mining": 0,
       "Foraging": 2,
       "Luck": 1,
       "Attack": 0,
       "Defense": 0,
       "Speed": 0,
       "MaxStamina": 0,
       "MagneticRadius": 0,
       "Immunity": 0
},[/code][b]5. Save and restart[/b]
Save the file and restart the game. Changes are not picked up mid-session. Tooltips update automatically to match whatever you set, so the descriptions always tell the truth about your own config.
If you break the JSON (a missing comma or bracket), SMAPI will warn you in the console and fall back to the default values. Deleting config.json and relaunching always regenerates a clean copy.
[b]Hats from other mods[/b]
Custom hats work exactly the same way. To find a custom hat's ID, wear it in game and press [b]F5[/b]. The ID is printed to the SMAPI console. Add it to config.json like any vanilla hat:
[code]"NewCoolHat": {
       "Farming": 0,
       "Fishing": 0,
       "Mining": 0,
       "Foraging": 0,
       "Luck": 0,
       "Attack": 2,
       "Defense": 1,
       "Speed": 1,
       "MaxStamina": 20,
       "MagneticRadius": 0,
       "Immunity": 0
},[/code]If it is added at the end of the file, make sure the "," is between the new hat and the last vanilla one. The last hat in the file should not have a trailing ",".[/spoiler]
